paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to take home. Some of the people in Israel were longing for the Day of the LORD, but Amos warns them, "It will be darkness and not light." (Amos 5:18) Wanting God to show up is good, but I can't want Him to show up while I ignore what He's already said. I'd be the guy at the door with a tray of burnt cookies, saying, "Surprise, I brought snacks!"

Look at what the LORD says about their feasts: "I hate, I despise your feasts!" (Amos 5:21) That's STRONG. Then He says what He wants instead: "But let justice roll on like a river, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream." (Amos 5:24) Not a puddle and not a Sunday trickle, but a river that doesn't quit.

So the question for you and me is simple: do my worship and my daily life point the same direction? The LORD calls out the idols they made for themselves (Amos 5:26), and then says, "Therefore I will send you into exile" (Amos 5:27). I keep my ovens ready for the Marriage Supper, and I want my whole life ready too, not just the part that sings. This isn't the end of the teaching, friend, so stay with me.
